summary: Full backend + UI verification of the HttpOnly cookie auth migration and the two frontend fixes (Monitor hook deps, DKA-CEC/HTCBT NewSample samples state refactor to {id, code}[]). 16/16 pytest cases pass. UI smoke of all 5 modules after login passes with 0 non-404 console errors. HttpOnly cookie elastech_session verified: not visible to JS (document.cookie), no elastech_token in localStorage, Set-Cookie carries HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=None. CORS preflight to /api/auth/login returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true with reflected Origin (NOT '*'). Logout clears cookie and invalidates /auth/me.

critical_code_review_comments: Legacy fallback header auth (X-Session-Token / Authorization: Bearer) is still accepted in _extract_token (server.py:91-96). Keep for the transition window, but plan to remove to avoid confusion once all clients are on the cookie.

SESSION_COOKIE is set with SameSite=None + Secure, which requires HTTPS everywhere. This is fine in the Emergent preview URL but will break if the app is ever served over plain HTTP (e.g., local dev without a TLS proxy). Document this.

CORS fallback uses allow_origin_regex='.*' + allow_credentials=True, which effectively opens credentialed CORS to any origin. Low risk for an internal admin tool but worth noting; preferred future state is an explicit allow-list via CORS_ORIGINS.
